topics.title: Subsequent Events - Concept and Classification
explain: Subsequent events are events occurring between the financial statements date and the date of auditor's report, plus facts known after the report date.
Financial reporting frameworks distinguish between two main types of subsequent events.
Type 1: Adjusting events provide evidence of conditions existing on the date of financial statements (e.g., bankruptcy of a debtor).
Type 2: Non-adjusting events provide evidence of conditions arising after the date of financial statements (e.g., loss due to fire).
SA 560 outlines auditor's responsibilities to ensure proper adjustment or disclosure of these events in financial statements.

flow.title: Categorizing Subsequent Events
steps: Check if condition existed at F.S. date
If No: Disclose in notes if material

topics.example: A debtor owing Rs. 50 lakhs is declared insolvent in May 2026 due to financial troubles existing in March 2026. This requires adjusting the provision in the financial statements.
remember: Adjusting events = conditions existed at F.S. date.
Non-adjusting events = conditions arose after F.S. date.
mistakes: Assuming all events occurring after the financial statements date require changing numbers in the financial statements.

quiz.q: A fire breaks out in May 2026 destroying inventory after the financial statements date of March 31, 2026. How should this be treated if going concern is unaffected?
o: Disclose in Notes to Accounts if material
quiz.why: It is a non-adjusting event arising after the F.S. date requiring disclosure if material.

quiz.q: What is the primary objective under SA 560 for events occurring before the auditor's report date?
o: Obtain evidence that events requiring adjustment/disclosure are appropriately reflected
quiz.why: The auditor must ensure all events needing adjustment or disclosure are properly reflected in F.S.

topics.title: Audit Procedures & Facts Known After Report Date
explain: Auditor must perform procedures covering the period up to the auditor's report date (reading minutes, latest interim F.S., inquiring management).
Auditor must request Written Representation under SA 580 that all subsequent events requiring adjustment/disclosure have been handled.
For facts known after report date but before F.S. issuance: auditor discusses with management, determines if F.S. need amendment, and inquires management's intentions.
If management amends F.S., auditor performs necessary procedures, extends procedures to new report date, and provides a new audit report.
If management refuses to amend F.S.: auditor modifies opinion (if report not yet provided) or takes steps to prevent reliance on report.

flow.title: Handling Facts Discovered Before F.S. Issuance
steps: If amended: Extend procedures & issue new report
If refused: Modify opinion or block report reliance

topics.example: After signing the audit report, the auditor learns of a major government subsidy approved for the audit year before F.S. are issued. Management amends F.S. and auditor issues a fresh audit report.
remember: New report date cannot be earlier than F.S. approval date.
Auditor has no active obligation to search for facts after report date.
mistakes: Thinking the auditor must perform active routine audit procedures after signing the audit report.

quiz.q: What should the auditor do if management refuses to amend financial statements for a material fact discovered before F.S. issuance (report not yet delivered to entity)?
o: Modify the opinion as required by SA 705
quiz.why: If the report is not yet provided to the entity, the auditor modifies the opinion under SA 705.

quiz.q: What is the rule regarding the date of a new auditor's report on amended financial statements?
o: Must be backdated to F.S. date
Cannot be earlier than date of approval of amended F.S.
Must match original audit report date
Can be any future date within 5 years
quiz.why: The new audit report date cannot be earlier than the approval date of the amended F.S.

topics.title: Meaning of Going Concern & Responsibilities
explain: Going concern is a fundamental accounting assumption where an entity is viewed as continuing operation for the foreseeable future.
Management must assess going concern appropriateness, covering at least 12 months from the financial statements date.
Auditor's responsibility: obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the appropriateness of management's use of going concern basis.
Auditor must conclude whether a material uncertainty exists related to events or conditions casting doubt on going concern.
The absence of reference to material uncertainty in audit report cannot be viewed as a guarantee of future viability.
topics.example: A company incurs net losses for 2 consecutive years but holds strong cash reserves and growing orders. Management prepares F.S. on going concern basis, which auditor finds appropriate.
remember: Management assessment period must be at least 12 months from F.S. date.
Audit report is not a guarantee of future solvency.
mistakes: Assuming any net loss automatically implies that the entity is not a going concern.

quiz.q: If management's assessment of going concern covers less than 12 months from F.S. date, what must the auditor do?
o: Request management to extend assessment to at least 12 months
quiz.why: Auditor must request management to cover at least 12 months from financial statements date.

quiz.q: Is an unmodified audit report a guarantee that the company will remain solvent for the next year?
o: No, audit cannot predict future events or act as guarantee
quiz.why: Inherent limitations mean absence of uncertainty reference cannot be viewed as a guarantee.

topics.title: Indicators of Doubt & Implications for Audit Report
explain: Indicators casting doubt include Financial (net current liability, negative cash flows), Operating (loss of key management/market), and Other (non-compliance with laws).
Additional procedures when doubt exists: analyze cash flow forecasts, review debenture/loan terms, inquire legal counsel, obtain Written Representation on future plans.
If use of Going Concern basis is inappropriate: express an Adverse Opinion.
If Going Concern basis is appropriate but material uncertainty exists AND adequately disclosed: express Unmodified Opinion with a separate 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' section.
If material uncertainty exists BUT NOT adequately disclosed: express Qualified or Adverse Opinion under SA 705.

flow.title: Audit Report Decision Matrix for Going Concern
steps: Check if Going Concern basis is appropriate
If Appropriate -> Check if Material Uncertainty exists
If Uncertainty exists & Disclosed -> Unmodified + Material Uncertainty Paragraph
If Uncertainty exists & Not Disclosed -> Qualified or Adverse Opinion

topics.example: Company defaults on all loans and faces imminent liquidation. Management still uses going concern basis without liquidation basis. Auditor issues an Adverse Opinion.
remember: Use of inappropriate basis = Adverse Opinion.
Adequately disclosed material uncertainty = Unmodified opinion + Material Uncertainty section.
mistakes: Using an Emphasis of Matter paragraph instead of 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' section when uncertainty is disclosed.

quiz.q: What audit opinion is required if management uses going concern basis, but auditor judges it to be inappropriate?
quiz.why: When use of going concern basis of accounting is inappropriate, auditor must express an Adverse Opinion.

quiz.q: How should an auditor report when material uncertainty exists regarding going concern, and management has provided full disclosure in notes?
o: Unmodified Opinion with 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' section
quiz.why: Proper disclosure results in unmodified opinion accompanied by a dedicated section.

topics.title: Evaluation of Misstatements Identified During Audit
explain: Auditor must accumulate all misstatements identified during audit, other than those clearly trivial.
Clearly trivial means matters that are wholly inconsequential, individually or in aggregate.
Auditor determines if overall strategy/plan needs revision if accumulated misstatements approach materiality.
Auditor must communicate misstatements on a timely basis to appropriate level of management and request correction.
Prior to evaluating uncorrected misstatements, auditor reassesses materiality set under SA 320 against actual financial results.
topics.example: Auditor finds machinery repair of Rs. 5 lakhs wrongly capitalized as an asset. Since it is not trivial, auditor accumulates it and requests management to correct it.
remember: Clearly trivial matters are not accumulated.
Reassess SA 320 materiality using actual financial figures before final evaluation.

quiz.q: Which misstatements are excluded from accumulation by the auditor under SA 450?
quiz.why: SA 450 specifies that auditor accumulates misstatements other than those clearly trivial.

quiz.q: What step must the auditor take before evaluating the effect of uncorrected misstatements?
o: Reassess materiality determined in accordance with SA 320
quiz.why: Auditor reassesses materiality to confirm if it remains appropriate for actual financial results.

topics.title: Uncorrected Misstatements, Representations & Documentation
explain: Auditor evaluates whether uncorrected misstatements are material, individually or in aggregate (considering size, nature, and prior period effects).
Auditor communicates uncorrected misstatements and their effect on opinion to TCWG, requesting correction.
Auditor must request Written Representation from management stating whether they believe effects of uncorrected misstatements are immaterial.
A summary of uncorrected misstatements must be included in or attached to the Written Representation.
Documentation under SA 450 includes: trivial amount threshold, accumulated misstatements & correction status, and conclusion on materiality.

flow.title: Handling Uncorrected Misstatements
steps: Evaluate impact on F.S. as a whole

topics.example: Management leaves an uncorrected error of Rs. 20,000 unadjusted. Management provides written representation stating they consider this uncorrected amount immaterial to F.S. as a whole.
remember: Written representation must contain or attach summary of uncorrected misstatements.
Audit documentation must record the clearly trivial threshold.
mistakes: Forgetting to attach the summary of uncorrected misstatements to management's representation letter.

quiz.q: What written representation must auditor request regarding uncorrected misstatements?
o: That all misstatements have been eliminated
That management believes uncorrected misstatements are immaterial to F.S. as a whole
That auditor is responsible for errors
quiz.why: Management represents whether they believe effects of uncorrected misstatements are immaterial.

quiz.q: Which of the following MUST be documented under SA 450?
o: Amount below which items are clearly trivial
quiz.why: SA 450 explicitly requires documenting the threshold amount for clearly trivial misstatements.

topics.title: Written Representations - Concept & Management Duties
explain: Written Representation is a written statement by management provided to auditor to confirm matters or support audit evidence.
It does NOT include financial statements, assertions therein, or supporting books and records.
Written representations are necessary audit evidence, but DO NOT provide sufficient appropriate evidence on their own.
Objectives of SA 580: obtain representations on fulfillment of management's responsibilities, support other evidence, and respond appropriately.
Management must confirm fulfillment of responsibility for F.S. preparation and that all transactions are recorded and provided to auditor.
topics.example: Management provides a signed representation letter confirming all sales transactions have been recorded. Auditor uses this to support corroborative evidence obtained during testing.
remember: Written representations are audit evidence, but NOT sufficient appropriate evidence on their own.
F.S. and accounting records are NOT written representations.
mistakes: Believing that getting a written representation allows the auditor to skip detailed audit testing.

quiz.q: Do written representations provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence on their own for matters they cover?
o: No, they provide necessary evidence but not sufficient appropriate evidence on their own
quiz.why: Written representations support evidence but cannot substitute for other necessary audit procedures.

quiz.q: Which of the following is considered a Written Representation under SA 580?
o: Management letter confirming completeness of information provided
quiz.why: F.S., assertions, and supporting records are excluded from the definition of written representations.

topics.title: Other Representations, Date, Form & Doubts on Reliability
explain: Other representations cover: suitability of accounting policies, plans affecting asset valuation, contingent liabilities, title to assets.
Qualifying language like 'to the best of knowledge and belief' can be accepted if management has appropriate responsibility and knowledge.
Date of representation must be as near as practicable to, but NOT AFTER, date of auditor's report.
Form: must be in form of a representation letter addressed to auditor.
If auditor doubts management's integrity or reliability of representation: perform procedures to resolve; if unresolved, re-evaluate integrity and consider Disclaimer of Opinion under SA 705.
If management refuses to provide representation on core responsibilities: auditor MUST disclaim opinion.

flow.title: Action when Representation is Refused
steps: Disclaim opinion under SA 705 if core representation missing

topics.example: Management refuses to sign written representation regarding F.S. preparation responsibility. Auditor issues a Disclaimer of Opinion under SA 705.
remember: Representation date: as near as practicable to, but NOT after, auditor's report date.
Refusal of core responsibilities representation = Disclaimer of Opinion.
mistakes: Dating the written representation letter after the date of the audit report.

quiz.q: What is the rule for dating a written representation letter relative to the audit report date?
o: Must be dated after audit report date
As near as practicable to, but not after, audit report date
Must be dated at beginning of financial year
Can be dated 30 days after audit report
quiz.why: Since auditor's opinion relies on representation, it cannot be dated after audit report date.

quiz.q: What opinion must auditor express if management refuses to provide written representations on fulfilling F.S. preparation responsibility?
quiz.why: SA 580 requires disclaimer of opinion if management fails to provide written representations on core responsibilities.

topics.title: Significance of Communication with TCWG
explain: Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) oversee strategic direction and accountability of entity (e.g., Board of Directors, Audit Committee).
Effective two-way communication develops constructive relationship, helps obtain relevant info, and assists TCWG in oversight.
Objectives of SA 260: communicate auditor's responsibilities, overview of planned scope/timing, significant findings, and promote two-way communication.
Matters to communicate: auditor's responsibilities, planned scope and timing (including significant risks), and significant findings.
For listed entities: auditor must also communicate written statements regarding auditor independence.

flow.title: SA 260 Communication Workflow
steps: Perform audit and note significant findings

topics.example: Auditor meets Audit Committee of a listed company to discuss major revenue recognition risks identified during scope planning.
remember: Independence communication is mandatory for listed entities.
Audit does not relieve management or TCWG of their responsibilities.
mistakes: Thinking communication with TCWG replaces the need to communicate with management.

quiz.q: For which entities is formal written communication of auditor's independence mandatory under SA 260?
quiz.why: SA 260 explicitly mandates written communication regarding independence in case of listed entities.

quiz.q: Does conducting an audit relieve management and TCWG of their financial reporting responsibilities?
o: No, audit does not relieve them of responsibilities
Only if auditor issues unmodified report
quiz.why: Audit of financial statements does not relieve management or TCWG of their responsibilities.

topics.title: Communication Process and Documentation
explain: Auditor communicates form, timing, and expected general content of communications with TCWG.
Significant findings must be communicated in writing if oral communication would not be adequate.
Auditor must evaluate whether two-way communication has been adequate for audit purposes.
If two-way communication is inadequate, auditor evaluates effect on risk assessment and ability to obtain evidence, taking appropriate action.
Documentation: oral communications must be documented in audit working papers (stating when and to whom), and copies of written communications must be retained.

flow.title: Documenting TCWG Communications
steps: If Written -> Retain copy in working papers
If Oral -> Record in audit notes with date and person

topics.example: Auditor verbally informs the Board about delays in receiving inventory confirmations, then notes the date, time, and attendees in audit documentation.
remember: Oral communications MUST record 'when' and 'to whom' it was said.
Written communications: retain full copy.
mistakes: Failing to document oral communications made to TCWG in audit files.

quiz.q: If matters required under SA 260 are communicated orally to TCWG, what must audit documentation include?
o: Details of when and to whom matters were communicated
quiz.why: Oral communications must be documented noting the time/date and the specific persons communicated with.

quiz.q: What should the auditor do if two-way communication with TCWG is evaluated as inadequate?
o: Evaluate effect on risk assessment & ability to obtain evidence
quiz.why: SA 260 requires auditor to evaluate how inadequate communication impacts risk assessment and evidence gathering.

topics.title: Communicating Internal Control Deficiencies
explain: Deficiency in internal control exists when a control cannot prevent/detect/correct misstatements timely, or a necessary control is missing.
Significant deficiency: a deficiency or combination of deficiencies that in auditor's judgment merits attention of TCWG.
Objective of SA 265: communicate appropriately to TCWG and management deficiencies of sufficient importance.
Significance depends on likelihood and potential magnitude of misstatement, not just whether misstatement actually occurred.
Indicators of significant deficiency include: ineffective control environment, management fraud, failure to remedy prior deficiencies, absence of risk assessment process.

flow.title: Identifying & Evaluating Control Deficiencies
steps: Identify internal control deficiency during audit
Evaluate likelihood and magnitude of potential misstatement
Determine if it constitutes a Significant Deficiency
If Significant -> Prepare written communication for TCWG

topics.example: Auditor notes company bypasses approval procedures for director-related party transactions. Auditor judges this as a significant deficiency in control over related party transactions.
remember: Significant deficiency is based on auditor's professional judgment.
Actual misstatement need not occur for a deficiency to be significant.
mistakes: Assuming SA 265 requires auditor to express an opinion on internal controls overall.

quiz.q: What is a 'significant deficiency in internal control' under SA 265?
o: Any error found in journal entries
Deficiency meriting attention of TCWG in auditor's professional judgment
quiz.why: SA 265 defines it as a deficiency or combination of deficiencies that merits the attention of TCWG.

quiz.q: Is an actual material misstatement required to occur for a deficiency to be classified as significant?
o: No, depends on likelihood and potential magnitude
quiz.why: Significance depends on potential magnitude and likelihood, even if no misstatement occurred yet.

topics.title: Communication Requirements & Structure under SA 265
explain: Auditor MUST communicate significant deficiencies in writing to TCWG on a timely basis.
Auditor must also communicate to management in writing significant deficiencies and other deficiencies deserving management's attention.
Written communication must contain: description of deficiencies, explanation of potential effects, and sufficient contextual information.

Contextual explanations required: audit purpose was to express F.S. opinion; internal control was considered to design procedures, not express control opinion; reported matters are limited to identified significant deficiencies.
One-liner statements without explaining potential effects or context are improper and non-compliant with SA 265.

flow.title: Structure of SA 265 Written Letter
steps: Explain potential effects on financial statements
Clarify audit purpose was F.S. opinion, not control opinion
State report is limited to deficiencies found during audit
Send timely written letter to TCWG and management

topics.example: Auditor sends formal letter describing missing physical inventory checks, explaining risk of inventory misstatement and profit error, and adding standard contextual disclaimers.
remember: Significant deficiencies MUST be communicated IN WRITING.
Must explain potential effects, not just state the issue in one line.
mistakes: Sending a simple one-line email stating the deficiency without explaining potential effects or audit context.

quiz.q: In what form must significant deficiencies in internal control be communicated to TCWG under SA 265?
quiz.why: SA 265 explicitly requires written communication of significant deficiencies to TCWG.

quiz.q: Which explanation must be included in the written communication under SA 265?
o: That audit guarantees all controls work perfectly
That audit consideration of internal control was not to express an opinion on control effectiveness
That management is relieved of internal control duties
That auditor will fix the controls
quiz.why: Auditor must clarify that internal control evaluation was for designing audit procedures, not expressing control opinion.
